title: PrjDelLiveAssessment
description: DGRF Operational Project Delivery Risk Assessment Schema for In-Flight Execution (Dimensions O1 - O5)

projectId.description: Unique identifier for the project evaluated

sprintOrMilestone.description: Current execution iteration, sprint, or phase milestone

o1_schedule.title: O1: Schedule Velocity & Milestone Variance
o1_schedule.description: Critical path slip rate and variance against planned baseline (Max 25 pts). 3: On schedule or tracking ahead (<5% variance, zero critical path slippage). 10: Manageable schedule variance (5-15% slippage, recoverable without baseline change). 18: Critical path delayed by 15-30%, compressed testing phase planned. 25: Uncontrolled critical path delay (>30%), repeated milestone re-baselining.

o2_acceptance.title: O2: Acceptance Testing & Defect Inflow
o2_acceptance.description: User acceptance test pass rates, defect backlog growth, and technical debt accumulation (Max 20 pts). 3: Defect closure rate exceeds inflow; UAT first-time pass rate > 90%. 8: Stable defect burn-down; manageable P2/P3 backlogs with workarounds. 14: Defect backlog increasing; recurring critical (P1) defects blocking acceptance. 20: Severe test failures, release blockers ignored, or testing bypassed to hit dates.

o3_capital_efficiency.title: O3: Capital Efficiency & Cost Variance (CPI/EVM)
o3_capital_efficiency.description: Earned Value Cost Performance Index (CPI) and burn rate sustainability (Max 20 pts). 3: Cost Performance Index (CPI) >= 0.98; expenditure matches delivered value. 8: CPI between 0.90 - 0.97; minor burn acceleration with identified remedy. 14: CPI between 0.75 - 0.89; persistent overspend without proportional value delivered. 20: CPI < 0.75; acute run-rate crisis requiring emergency budget replenishment.

o4_team_morale.title: O4: Team Morale & Key-Person Attrition Risk
o4_team_morale.description: Engineering burnout, psychological safety, and attrition in key architecture/lead roles (Max 15 pts). 2: High team cohesion, sustainable cadence, zero key departures, high psychological safety. 6: Occasional overtime during release crunches; stable core team. 11: Chronic crunch (>55 hrs/wk), elevated cynicism, key leads expressing flight intent. 15: Critical talent departures, toxic blame culture, unmitigated key-person single points of failure.

o5_reporting_truth.title: O5: Reporting Transparency & Status Candor (The Watermelon Effect)
o5_reporting_truth.description: Truthfulness of executive dashboard status vs engineering ground reality (Max 20 pts). 3: Radical transparency; failures and risks surfaced immediately without reprisal. 8: Balanced reporting; minor negative indicators smoothed but key impediments escalated. 14: Visible 'Watermelon Effect' (Green on exterior dashboards, Red inside engineering teams). 20: Actively manipulated or suppressed metrics, gag orders on bad news, fabricated RAG statuses.
